newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian MTBE - Demand thin but supported by gasoline.
newsitem.headline: Asian MTBE - Demand thin but supported by gasoline.

text.p: Asian spot MTBE prices were supported by firm gasoline prices but current high levels might attract arbitrage cargoes resulting in a build in inventories, industry sources said on Wednesday.
Singapore free-on-board (fob) end March-early April MTBE was being assessed in a wide range between $268-$275 per tonne, with trade heard as high at $275.
One 2,000 tonne parcel was sold to a Singapore refiner at $280 on a cost-and-freight basis for delivery in end March, a producer said.
"It is purely attributable to the strength of the gasoline market," said a supplier on the high deal levels.
Good demand and tightness in the Asian gasoline market last week pushed the 95-octane grade over $29.00 per barrel, fob Singapore.
But some MTBE traders were bearish on the outlook.
"The market is now the best in the world, and suppliers will tend to allocate more volume into this region," a supplier said.
"It is progressively getting weaker," one trader said on the MTBE market. "Inventories will be higher as demand is not that active."
Sources said demand from blenders was weak with Taiwan last week only buying by tender two 250,000-barrel cargoes of 95-octane reformate with 2-percent MTBE for first-half April delivery.
They said the blending demand for this purchase would only amount to 5,000 tonnes of MTBE.
"It is very small compard to the system here of around 50 to 70,000 tonnes," a trader said.
But a source at Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) denied high stocks in Singapore.
He said the start-up of the 700,000-tone-per-year Saudi Petroleum Co (SADAF) plant has been delayed from March to April, but did not give the reason.
But some traders said last week's Taiwan's MTBE purchase was reflective of the market.
"CPC's award at a low of $280 is an indication that producers are eager to place barrels," a trader said.

Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) last week bought 7,000 tonnes of MTBE for April 6-20 delivery at $280-$283 per tonne cost-and-freight Taiwan, from Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC).
